title: Add unit/integration tests to prevent output-token metering regressions (streaming/tool calls/truncation)
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Problem
Output-token under/over-counting has been a recurring failure mode, especially on the streaming code path. This directly corrupts the primary unit economics KPI (blended $/1M output tokens) and breaks reconciliation vs billing. We need automated coverage that fails fast when token metering diverges from the actual emitted content.

Scope
Add unit + integration tests that validate output_tokens metering for:
1) Streaming responses (SSE/chunked) including boundary cases
2) Tool/function calling responses (arguments emitted via tool_calls)
3) Truncation / stop conditions (max_output_tokens, stop sequences, context limit behavior)

Non-goals
- Re-define the metering algorithm (handled in ENG-8421 / related PRs)
- Add new dashboard queries or warehouse logic

Why this matters (Unit Economics)
The dashboard’s denominator is output tokens. Any silent metering regression changes $/1M output tokens with no underlying cost change, causing false regressions and breaking Finance signoff.

Acceptance criteria
- Tests fail if metered output_tokens differs from a reference count computed from the exact bytes/strings emitted to the client.
- Coverage includes: streaming, tool calls, truncation/stops, and early client disconnect.
- Tests run in CI on every change to gateway/runtime metering code paths.
- Add at least one “canary-style” test that mimics the production streaming path (similar to perf-canary PR-455) to catch regressions that unit tests miss.

Test plan
A) Unit tests (gateway metering library)
- Tokenize-and-count matches reference tokenizer for:
  - plain text content
  - multi-chunk concatenation (simulate chunk boundaries splitting UTF-8 sequences and wordpieces)
  - tool call payloads (function name + arguments) counted consistently with product definition (count what is emitted to the user)
  - stop sequence handling (stop token excluded/included per definition; assert expected behavior explicitly)
- Explicit fixtures for:
  - empty final chunk
  - final chunk with finish_reason only
  - repeated partial deltas with no text change

B) Integration tests (API-level)
Add e2e tests in the API test harness that:
- Call the chat/generate endpoint in streaming mode; capture the full SSE transcript; reconstruct the final emitted content.
- Compare:
  - metering field in response metadata (output_tokens)
  - metering field emitted via metrics/event (if available in test env)
  - reference count from reconstructed emitted content
- Cases:
  1. streaming=true, no tools, 2–3 short chunks
  2. streaming=true, long output that spans many chunks (ensure boundary coverage)
  3. tool calling: model returns tool_calls; arguments are streamed in deltas; ensure counting is stable
  4. truncation: set max_output_tokens low and assert finish_reason + count
  5. stop sequences: include a stop string and assert whether the stop text is counted (pin the expected behavior)
  6. early client disconnect: terminate stream mid-way; ensure we do NOT emit misleading output_tokens for a completion that wasn’t fully delivered (or assert the agreed definition)

Notes / open questions to resolve in this ticket
- Definition: Do we count tokens that were generated server-side but never delivered due to client disconnect? Current dashboard intent is “meter what we served/delivered.” Align with Nadia + Finance if ambiguity remains.
- Tool calls: Confirm whether tool call arguments should count as output tokens in the same bucket as natural language output (current working assumption: yes, if it’s part of the model output we stream back).

Implementation notes
- Prefer golden fixtures with deterministic model output. Avoid flakey “live model” tests.
- If needed, use a stubbed model backend that emits a fixed sequence of deltas (including tool_call deltas) so we can validate metering deterministically.
- Add helper: reconstruct_emitted_text_and_tool_payload(stream_events) -> string used for reference tokenization.

Links
- Related fix: ENG-8421 Add output token metering to streaming path
- Related work: sources/github/redwood/pr-19355-streaming-output-token-metering-fix.json
- Canary precedent: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-455-add-canary-check-for-output-token-metering.json
- Context: SUP-28501 streaming output token metering under-count

Rollout
- Land unit tests first (fast, cheap signal)
- Add integration tests behind CI job flag if runtime is heavy; graduate to default once stable

Risks
- Discrepancies due to tokenizer version drift. Pin tokenizer version in test harness and assert it in logs.
- Ambiguity in what constitutes “delivered” for streaming if clients disconnect. Must codify behavior now to avoid future churn.
comments: 2025-02-06 (Nadia Rahman): Creating this as a follow-up to the streaming undercount incident. We need CI coverage that would have caught the regression before rollout. Please make sure we cover tool-calls + truncation too; those paths also bypass some of the shared helpers.

2025-02-10 (Felix Schneider): Drafted unit test fixtures for chunk boundary behavior + empty final chunk. Found current helper double-counts when a delta repeats the same content (rare but possible); filed note to confirm expected semantics before encoding in tests.

2025-02-12 (Allison Grant): +1 on early disconnect case. For observability we should avoid emitting a misleading “completion” metric if the stream is cut. Even if we still log generated tokens somewhere, the dashboard denominator should be served tokens.

2025-02-14 (Chloe Martin): Please ensure integration tests exercise the exact gateway streaming path (SSE framing + buffering). We’ve had regressions that unit tests missed due to the streaming adapter.

2025-02-18 (Felix Schneider): Opened PR with unit tests + stubbed streaming backend for deterministic integration tests. Remaining question: counting of stop sequence text is currently inconsistent between non-streaming vs streaming; I pinned to ‘exclude stop string from output’ per Nadia’s guidance, but flagging for confirmation in review.
